notes:
Summary: enterprise procurement focused on Dedicated reserved GPUs for latency-sensitive trading assistant. Customer extremely sensitive to maintenance windows and downtime during market hours. Primary negotiation topics: uptime %, credits, scheduled maintenance rules, and support SLAs.

Key technical requirements (shorthand):
- Workload: synchronous chat for traders + embeddings for risk vectors + nightly reranking jobs.
- Throughput targets: baseline sustained throughput ~350 concurrent chat sessions; burst to 800 for market open.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 80ms (short prompts), p95 target <= 250ms; negotiation on p99 for long seqs.
- Reserved capacity: initial commit 4x A100 equiv (baseline), plan to scale to 12x within 6 months if SLA latency holds. Quant plan: prefer transpiled FP16/INT8 quant profiles for cost.

SLA negotiation highlights (conversation snippets + AE notes):
- Baikal legal: "we need 99.99% uptime for production trading — anything less exposes us to material loss". AE/Maya note: customer understands cost delta; open to graduated credits but pushing high bar.
- Redwood proposed credit schedule (current draft v3): uptime >=99.99% = no credits; 99.95-99.99 = 10% monthly credit; 99.9-99.95 = 25% credit; <99.9 = 50% credit. Baikal pushing for stronger remedies above 99.99.
- Maintenance windows: Baikal requests maintenance only in pre-market windows (02:00-05:00 ET) and 72h advance notice; Redwood wants monthly 2-hour window; negotiation in progress to carve out market-open blackout periods.
- Support response: P1 (prod outage affecting trading) target 15 min response + 1h remediation SLA; P2 (degraded perf) 1h response; P3 4h. Baikal insist on dedicated escalation path and named SE in rotations.

Open technical/legal action items:
- Legal to propose alternate credit scaling if Greenwood (Redwood) can provide rollback-to-previous-model guaranteed fallback during incidents (reduces Baikal credit demand).
- SE (Diego) to provide quantized perf numbers for 8x A100 equiv by 2024-11-10 (deliverable: perf matrix + expected p95/p99 under mixed load).
- Security to provide KMS/HSM integration plan and timeline; Baikal requires HSM-backed keys in VPC before production go-live.
- Procurement asked for runbook demonstrating failover to secondary region (latency impact analysis).

POC milestones / acceptance criteria:
- Week 1: provision reserved 4x pool, validate p95 latency under synthetic trading load (target <=250ms).
- Week 2: 48-hour soak under burst pattern, no more than 1 incident causing >5% increase in p95 latency.
- Week 3: security review sign-off + KMS test keys in staging.

Stated next steps (short):
- Send redline to SLA v3 w/ proposed uptime compromise (99.975%) + alternative remediation (option for escalation credits + short-term free capacity extension).
- Diego to attach perf matrix and model-variant fallback plan by 2024-11-10.
- Legal sync w/ Baikal counsel week of 2024-11-04.

Misc notes:
- Customer mentioned competing bids from Anthropic + internal infra team; decision sensitive to both cost and operational guarantees.
- Procurement flagged requirement for 12-month minimum term for pricing to apply.
- Quote: "We can tolerate brief maintenance if we get guaranteed rollback and a transparent credit policy" — Head of Ops (call 2024-10-28).
